framing.description: Architecture-matched §5.8 privacy-cost re-measurement (this session). Both binaries are local-circuit-only (encrypt..decrypt, no gRPC), share vendor_server/include/rotation_hoisting.h, and differ ONLY in ctx.params.coeff_modulus: 200-bit {60,40,40,60} (vendor_server/build/benchmark, CKKSContext) vs 160-bit {60,40,60} (vendor_server/build/benchmark_160, CKKSContext160). strategy=fold is the deployed reduction strategy. Both are OUT OF TCB (hold a live secret key for self-timing only); see ckks_context.h / ckks_context_160.h.
framing.supersedes: artifacts/privacy_cost_analysis.json's latency_us field, which measured vendor_server_main (200-bit, legacy decrypt-capable CKKSContext-in-RPC-service) vs vendor_server_160 (160-bit, eval-only EvalContext160) -- a different-server-architecture confound documented in AUDIT.md. That file's bandwidth_bytes and precision_max_abs_error fields are NOT superseded (they are functions of the modulus chain, not the binary, and remain valid).

key_finding: Architecture-matched (same codebase, same rotation_hoisting.cpp, same strategy=fold, differ only in coeff_modulus): one additional 40-bit RNS prime (200-bit vs 160-bit chain) costs +6763.3us (97.4%) median latency (Mann-Whitney p=0.00e+00), measured under cpu_governor='performance'. This supersedes the deployed-binary delta, which mixed this cost with an unrelated server-architecture difference -- see artifacts/privacy_cost_analysis.json's 'deployed_cross_architecture_e2e_delta_DEPRECATED' field for that figure, kept for transparency, not for citation.
